element.name: Web Hosting
element.documentation: The static-site hosting node common to both samples (sample-azure's Static Web App, sample-gcp's Firebase Hosting) — serves the Frontend's static files and the app's runtime config to the Visitor's browser.

element.name: Database
element.documentation: The managed database node common to both samples (sample-azure's Azure SQL Server, sample-gcp's Cloud Firestore) — hosts the one seeded collection/table and the database engine that executes queries against it.

element.name: Visitor's Browser
element.documentation: The Visitor's web browser and the machine it runs on — where the Frontend executes, identical in role across both samples.

element.name: Demo Items Store
element.documentation: The persisted demo-items collection/table common to both samples (sample-azure's appdb dbo.DemoItems, sample-gcp's (default) database's demoItems collection) — created and seeded on first use.

element.name: App Config
element.documentation: Runtime configuration served by the hosting node and read by the Frontend at runtime, common to both samples (sample-azure's Database Config app setting, sample-gcp's Firebase Web Config) — identifies how to reach the Database, not itself a secret or an access control.

element.name: Internet
element.documentation: The open internet, through which the Visitor's browser reaches the hosting node and (directly or by way of a mediating API, depending on the sample) the Database — common to both samples' public, unauthenticated ingress path.

element.name: Web App Interface
element.documentation: Interface exposed by the web hosting node for external communication.

element.name: Database Interface
element.documentation: Interface exposed by the Database node for external communication — sample-azure's SQL Server (TDS) interface, sample-gcp's Firestore API interface.

element.name: Database Engine
element.documentation: The database engine behind the Database node, common to both samples (sample-azure's SQL Server Database Engine, sample-gcp's Firestore Database Engine) — executes queries sent through the Database Interface.

element.name: Web Hosting Service
element.documentation: The hosting node's own serving software, common to both samples (sample-azure's Static Web App Hosting Service, sample-gcp's Firebase Hosting Service) — serves the Frontend's static files and provisions App Config to the Visitor's browser.

element.name: Frontend
element.documentation: Static browser app common to both samples — loads the demo items on page load and renders the returned rows.

element.name: Initialize Demo Data
element.documentation: First-use setup common to both samples: creates the demo item store if it doesn't exist yet and inserts the seed items if it is empty, guarded so concurrent first loads seed only once.

element.name: Read Demo Items
element.documentation: Reads all demo items ordered by Id, on every page load — identical role in both samples.

element.name: DemoItems
element.documentation: The stored demo items — created and seeded on first use by Initialize Demo Data (app-init-demo-data).

element.name: Frontend Interface
element.documentation: HTTP interface exposed by the Frontend component for the Visitor to interact with.

element.name: Visitor
element.documentation: End user browsing the deployed web app.

element.name: View Demo Items
element.documentation: The Visitor loads the page and sees the demo item list (includes "Initialize demo data").

element.name: Website
element.documentation: The public URL/browser channel through which the Visitor reaches the app.

element.name: Demo Item
element.documentation: The business concept of an inventory item (Id, Name, Category) the Visitor views — the business-relevant counterpart of the stored demo items (do-demo-items).

element.name: Demo Items Table
element.documentation: The rendered items table — the perceptible form of Demo Item the Visitor actually reads.

element.name: Unprotected Data at Rest
element.documentation: The Demo Items Store (artifact-demo-items-store) and the storage media underlying the Database node (node-database) hold the persisted demo items without cryptographic confidentiality or integrity protection — a weakness exploitable, for either concern, by anyone with access to the underlying storage/media, independent of the application-level access controls in front of the Database Interface.

element.name: Storage Media Theft or Exfiltration
element.documentation: A threat actor obtains the Database node's underlying storage media, or exfiltrates a raw copy of it (backup, snapshot, decommissioned disk), bypassing the Database Interface and its application-level access controls entirely, to read its contents (a confidentiality threat).

element.name: Unauthorized Direct Modification of Stored Data
element.documentation: A threat actor with access to the Database node's underlying storage medium (not through the Database Interface or its application-level access controls — e.g. a compromised storage/backup administrator, or direct access to the raw files) alters the persisted demo items in place (an integrity threat).

element.name: Unauthorized Disclosure of Information at Rest
element.documentation: The risk that information held at rest in the Demo Items Store becomes readable to a party without authorization, because it was never protected independently of the application's own access controls (confidentiality; NIST SC-28(1) assessment objective sc-28.1_obj-1).

element.name: Unauthorized Modification of Information at Rest
element.documentation: The risk that information held at rest in the Demo Items Store is altered by a party without authorization, undetected, because it was never integrity-protected independently of the application's own access controls (integrity; NIST SC-28(1) assessment objective sc-28.1_obj-2).

element.name: SC-28(1) Cryptographic Protection
element.documentation: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of the following information at rest on system components or media: the demo items store (NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0, SC-28(1)) — one requirement, explicitly covering both the confidentiality (disclosure) and integrity (modification) concerns.

element.name: Control: Cryptographic Protection of Data at Rest
element.documentation: The organizational control that implements SC-28(1) — encrypting the Demo Items Store's underlying storage, closing the Unprotected Data at Rest vulnerability for both of SC-28(1)'s assessment objectives. In both sample-azure and sample-gcp (sample-oscal's own README.md "Results"), only the confidentiality objective (sc-28.1_obj-1) is actually satisfied today — encryption-at-rest is enabled, but neither sample's storage is tamper-evident, so the integrity objective (sc-28.1_obj-2) is open (see each sample's own POA&M). The "mitigates" relationship to risk-unauthorized-modification-data-at-rest below records that gap rather than overstating this control as fully closing it.

property.value: open — neither sample-azure nor sample-gcp's storage is tamper-evident yet (sc-28.1_obj-2 unmet; see each sample's own POA&M)
